title: Gate claims 'usage exit 2' but `!` inverts ANY non-zero exit to green — wrong exit codes or crashes pass
evidence:
+      # the r3-N7 pin: a bogus arg must be REJECTED (usage exit 2) — if the
+          tools/harness.sh input-parity && [ -x ./bin/harness ] && ! ./bin/harness input-parity bogus >/dev/null 2>&1
detail: The comment contracts rejection with usage exit 2, but the negation accepts any non-zero exit: a regression to exit 1 (crash) or 143 stays green, and if the suite ever runs before arg validation, real parity failures are masked by the `!`.
recommended_fix: Capture the exit code and assert it equals 2, e.g. `./bin/harness input-parity bogus >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?; [ $rc -eq 2 ]`, so only the documented usage-exit contract (not any failure) satisfies the pin.

title: pipe_demolish_btn_center re-duplicates the midpoint anchor math that the PR's own N2-r4 fold just single-sourced
detail: N2-r4 removed the hand-duplicated anchor math in favor of rnd.pipe_anchor, yet the new harness helper re-copies `(a.x+b.x)/2` instead of calling pipe_anchor with the fixture topology; a future anchor change silently drifts the test's press point from the app's.
recommended_fix: Pass the fixture topology into pipe_demolish_btn_center and delegate to rnd.pipe_anchor(view, topo, 0) — the single source the fold established — keeping the harness aligned with the render by construction.

title: Every dpad step forces sel_pipe = -1, destroying a mouse-made pipe selection on pad input
detail: Both mirror branches unconditionally set sel_pipe = -1, so a pipe selected via mouse/touch loses its demolish popover the moment the player nudges the dpad — consistent with click-select exclusivity, but a cross-device side effect not flagged in the diff.
recommended_fix: Document the interaction in the decision log, or gate the mirror to only touch the selection when the dpad step actually moves the cursor, so a mouse-made pipe selection survives incidental pad input.
